item.title: SCP Draft: The Consuming Mould: Re: SCP Draft: The Consuming Mould
item.content:encoded:
This idea has been done quite a few times before, virus, end of the world, don't let it escape. What makes yours different? I advise you to check out SCP-1462 as it has a similar effect as yours. My critiques and final thoughts will be included in several collapsibles below.

Critiques
Critiques

The container must be completely synthetic, and must be cleared of any organic matter, aside from SCP-XXX itself, any time that the container is opened.

You should remove the comma between synthetic & and. You do not need a comma there because you have the word and there. Commas only need to be put before the word and if there is a list of three or more items or ideas. Instead format that sentence like this.

The container must be made of completely synthetic materials and must be cleared of any organic matter, aside from SCP-XXX itself, any time that the container is opened.

Lower clearances may enter, but only if accompanied by a level 3.

Level three what? Ogre?

attempted termination of any subjects.

I don't think that the foundation would use an unknown disease to kill people. They would kill by firing squad. If they really wanted to use an scp they would just use 173 or something. Why risk a containment breach on something that can be done with a lot less work.

To enter the wall, personnel must have level 2 clearance or higher.

This should just be removed entirely. When a sentence is marked out there should be something after it that actually pertains to what the crossed out sentence was saying. Rather after yours you continue to explain stuff that has nothing to do with the prior sentence.

access for personnel of level 3 clearance or above only, as to prevent any SCP-XXXX-A or SCP-XXXX-B instances from breaking out and wreaking havoc.

I would change the level clearance to level 4 if no experimentation or research is allowed as level three is just senior research personnel. Level four personnel are senior administrators tasked with keeping the foundation secure and preventing containment breaches.

Sorry for only critiquing your containment procedures but your article is rather long. Even though I couldn't give you tips on the rest I hope that this helps.

-

Final thoughts
Final Thoughts

I see this theme of virus SCPs pop up quite often. Here is a list of a few and it can be very hard to take these common themes and make it interesting. I want you to read a few of these articles that have to do with viruses and take note of what you like and dislike about each. I also want to know what you will do for a plot line. In my opinion doing a virus/fungus SCP is so overdone it's going to be hard to make yours interesting and stand out from the rest. Good news is that there is an audience for everything. Definitely reach out to more experienced writers and critiquers for their thoughts as they will be a lot more helpful than I am and can help you set an interesting plot to go with the article. I hope you do well in your creative writing endeavors and have a good day!

item.title: Lost in the Fog / Temporal SCP: Re: Lost in the Fog / Temporal SCP
item.content:encoded:
Asked to crit via IRC. Please keep in mind I am not an official critter.

crit
hide crit

First off, this is a beautifully formatted draft. I'd remove the top "Classified by the authority of the SCP Foundation" header though. It doesn't add anything and is needlessly distracting.

Second, the description of the items is a little hard to understand. You state it's a weather phenomenon that forms from the fog, but then you later state that it's a Class II temporal anomaly, so which one is it?

Some line by line:

A Foundation meteorological team is to be stationed at Site-287 at all times, which is to receive additional staffing during the spring and autumn, as there is an increased risk of manifestations during these periods.

Remove everything after autumn. You'll want the reader to see that the site is to receive additional staffing during spring and autumn, wonder why, and continue reading to find out. There's also usually no reason to explain why containment procedures are needed in the ConProc section itself.

All efforts should be focused on predicting the precise times of SCP-XXXX manifestations. To achieve this, teams should analyze data on climate and weather patterns from national weather forecasting institutions, as well as from their own instrumentation.

This would read better as "All efforts should be focused on predicting the precise times of upcoming SCP-XXXX manifestations by analyzing data on climate and weather patterns." It's already implied the weather paterns are coming from forecasting instituations and that they'll be using their own instruments (whose else would they be using?).

During a NOTD event, MTF Epsilon-8 ("Mist Watchers") is to be dispatched to cordon off Dillon Dam Rd under the cover story of unfinished construction work. A security perimeter should be established within a 15-kilometer radius of the anomaly until it has dissipated.

Personal preference, but "Dillon Dam Rd" should be spelled out fully as "Dillon Dam Road", and "cover story" should be "falsified premise" or even just "premise". Also, and instances of "should be" work better as "will be".

In the fall

You used "autumn" before, I recommend remaining consistent.

from the nearby lake

You already identified the lake as being adjacent to the road, so "from the lake" works fine.

In each instance that the Foundation observed the anomaly's formation process, the fog drifted from the lake and moved toward the road, settling into its standard location for its usual duration.

Change to "During each manifestation, fog was observed moving from the lake to the road before settling."

Since this presents a clear risk to the safety of the local populace, Dillon Dam Rd is monitored at all times from a nearby observational facility designated as Site-287.

Staff have been disguised as civilian weathermen stationed there by NOAA4 under the guise of assisting local news stations in researching atmospheric and weather-related phenomena.

The installation is equipped with telemetering devices for collecting all relevant levels of meteorological data within 12 km, such as temperature, precipitation, and wind.

MTF Epsilon-8 is currently stationed at this facility and on standby in the likely scenario that a NOTD event occurs.

The perimeter is enclosed by a chain-link fence and patrolled constantly by armed security guards. Entry is only allowed to Level-3 personnel via access keycard.

Any trespassers are usually apprehended, questioned, and then given Class-B amnestics before being released.

These are procedures for containing SCP-XXXX, so they should be under "Containment Procedures".

Quadraginta already touched base on your logs and I agree with what they said in regards to that.

The idea and story are there, but are brought down by over-explanation and extraneous information that has either been stated earlier in the draft or doesn't relate to containment or the anomaly itself. There's some good parts and some bad parts, but you're definitely onto something here.

item.title: Kamikaze mosquitoes: Re: Kamikaze mosquitoes
item.content:encoded:
Asked to review via IRC. Please keep in mind I am an author / reader, not an official critter.

Crit
hide

The area in which SCP-XXXX is found in the wild is guarded by a perimeter.

A perimeter as in what? I think of a chain-link fence when I read this, but that wouldn't be able to contain mosquitoes.

All personnel by the perimeter must wear hazmat suits or other equipment that fully covers one's person. Also, you reference the area in the article again so it might be useful to give it a designation such as "Research Site-XXXX" or something.

All personnel by the perimeter must wear hazmat suits or other equipment that fully covers one's person.

Weird wording here. Try "All personnel assigned to [designated area] must wear provided personal protective equipment at all times." You could then put a footnote here outlining what that equipment specifically is.

Personnel on neighboring sites from any level that must be terminated, Agents of groups hostile to the Foundation, and D-class may be used for this. Cause of death: Termination by SCP-XXXX.

This is an unneeded tidbit of info. I would just change the sentence before this to say "D-Class individuals".

Outdated Containment Procedures: If personnel survives an attack of SCP-XXXX, wounds need to be tended and an antihistamine cream must be applied to their skin. Medical staff needs to check for infections1 and remove possible foreign objects from the body. Infected personnel needs to be isolated until they have tested negative twice in succession.

The outdated ConProcs are a weird thing to have in the article. Wouldn't they just remove the outdated ones so that there's no confusion?

SCP-XXXX refers to a species of mosquito that only exists in the Ratargul Swamp Forest in Bangladesh.

Instead of "that only exists", try "whose habitat ranges across".

After several attacks, SCP-XXXX got taxonomically classified as the Aedes kamikaze.

Change "attacks" to encounters, change "got" to "was". Remove "the".

Larvae and pupae of SCP-XXXX mainly eat honeydew, nectar, and other plant juices until they become adults. Adult specimens suck blood from wildlife which includes but is not limited to; several primates, birds, and smaller lizards. Unlike normal mosquitoes, males from SCP-XXXX also suck blood.

This whole piece can be boiled down to "SCP-XXXX display behavior patterns identical to that of non-anomalous specimens, with the exception of male specimens seeking blood as a food source.

Upon smelling blood or observing humans, specimens will become excited and less predictable. This behavior has been described as if they are experiencing heavy withdrawal symptoms from addiction or as if they are going insane. This climaxes in specimens charging towards the individual (often accompanied with a battle cry), losing maneuverability due to their high speed, and crashing into their target or an object resulting in dead on impact. Specimens also show this behavior when they are about to release offspring or reach the end of their lifecycle.

Nothing much here, but you can continue this from the previous statement. For example "Upon detecting living humans or any amount of human blood, however, SCP-XXXX's behavior will deviate greatly from any known species of Culicidae."

I'm going to generalize for the addendums from here on out:

Alright, so your addendums are obviously where the meat of story is and do a good job of fleshing out SCP-XXXX to be more than just "killer mosquitoes". My biggest criticism of them is that they are intimidating. Generally, a wall of text will discourage the reader from continuing to read unless you're amazing at keeping someone's attention. I'd take a look back through your addendums and remove / revise any information provided during the logs that the reader can reasonably deduce themselves or that was already stated previously in the description and containment procedures.

Next individuals up for termination by SCP-XXXX: deathbygin and D-3607.

Guess I'd better put on my gear ;)

item.title: Yin and Yang: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
just_a_doctor,

As per the Draft Forum Policies, new authors are to get their concepts reviewed and greenlighted by two experienced reviewers on the Idea Critique Forums before posting on the Draft Critique Forums.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can give assistance in developing an idea before a draft is written. They can also assist in letting you know if something similar exists on the site already, or inform you of various clichés/pitfalls to be cautious of. These elements are more effectively addressed earlier in the writing process.

If you would like to request a draft review without greenlights, you can use the IRC Chatrooms to solicit critique.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note the thread in which you received them, or the users whom provided them.

item.title: Tale: Unknown Angel: Re: Tale: Unknown Angel
item.content:encoded:
How can I imply that 06-M was at some point a component of 315? A tough question.

Hmm. Maybe it'd be enough to like, introduce the idea that 315 is the kinda thing that can have components? It feels…weird. To be honest; I'm not necessarily sure that this actually needs fleshed out more? Like I don't get the implications but I think it's fine cos it helps add to the feeling here of everything being kinda surreal and weird?

Secondly, I agree with Polly being introduced too late. Do you think this could be rectified by having the glassed agent be one of the three that are introduced in the first chat log, or is it kind of an inevitable problem of how brief the tale is in its current form and where the death is placed? If it is the latter I guess this just needs to be quite a bit longer.

It might help? Possibly just using the one chat log featuring Polly to show what she's like more and like…really capture the idea of her being a fresh faced newbie would help?

item.title: SCP Draft: Extra-Dimensional Vacuum Cleaner: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.
